limitations: Regions are approximate latitude/longitude boxes, not political borders; some boxes overlap.
Each grid cell is 2 x 2 degrees (about 220 km), so local details are not visible.

Temperature comes from a reanalysis (MERRA-2), evapotranspiration, runoff and soil moisture from a land surface model (GLDAS Noah), and precipitation from a satellite-gauge estimate (GPM IMERG); none is a direct measurement at every place, and the three sources differ in how they are made.

Trends are monotonic (Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope) over the stated period only; a change that rises and then falls can show as no significant trend, and a sudden jump (for example a change of satellite) can look like a trend.
Statistically significant does not mean large or important, and a trend says nothing about its cause.
Regional means average only the cells of a region that have data in at least 95% of the months, the same cells every month; land-only variables cover only the land part of a region.

Neighbouring grid cells on the trend maps are correlated. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control used on the maps is proven only for independent or positively dependent tests, so here it holds approximately: a single map can have more or fewer than 5% false discoveries. trendkit's Monte Carlo test measured a false discovery proportion of 0.059 +/- 0.007 (mean of 40 synthetic maps, target 0.05), but its synthetic cells were independent of each other, so it does not measure the effect of spatial correlation.

methods.autocorrelation_note: Yue and Wang (2004) variance correction with an AR(1) model, floored at 1; recommended in trendkit docs/METHODS.md
methods.data_requirement: at least 10 years of valid months and at least 80% of months valid (trendkit)
methods.deseasonalizing: monthly climatology subtracted per cell and per regional series
methods.display_series: monthly anomalies and a trailing 12-month running mean (null until 12 valid months); no annual means are published because the last year is incomplete

evidence_classes.coverage_cap: when the fixed mask covers less than 30% of the region box, strong and moderate become weak
evidence_classes.insufficient data: no regional report, or fewer than 10 years or 80% of months with data
evidence_classes.maps: grid cells use the same thresholds with the Benjamini-Hochberg q-value in place of p; cells that fail the data requirement are insufficient data
evidence_classes.moderate: p < 0.05 and the 95% confidence interval excludes 0 (not strong)
evidence_classes.strong: p < 0.01 and the 95% confidence interval of the slope excludes 0
evidence_classes.weak: p < 0.1 (not moderate or strong), or p < 0.05 with a confidence interval that includes 0

fdr.spatial_dependence: Neighbouring grid cells on the trend maps are correlated. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control used on the maps is proven only for independent or positively dependent tests, so here it holds approximately: a single map can have more or fewer than 5% false discoveries. trendkit's Monte Carlo test measured a false discovery proportion of 0.059 +/- 0.007 (mean of 40 synthetic maps, target 0.05), but its synthetic cells were independent of each other, so it does not measure the effect of spatial correlation.

methods.magnitude: slope_per_decade and total_change (slope x period years / 10) in the variable's units; standardized_change = total_change / residual_sd, where residual_sd is the standard deviation of the deseasonalized monthly regional series after removing the Sen trend line (no unit: how many typical monthly swings the trend added up to). Limits: not a measure of importance; smaller for noisy variables and larger for big regions, so compare variables within one region, not regions; smaller than the same measure on annual means; grows with the period length. No percent-of-mean is given (meaningless for temperature in degC).

orderings.by_evidence: evidence class (strong, moderate, weak, none, insufficient data); ties: smaller regional p-value, then larger |standardized_change|, then variable id
orderings.by_magnitude: larger |standardized_change| first, results without one last; ties: stronger evidence class, then smaller p-value, then variable id

methods.ranking: rank follows by_evidence: evidence class (strong, moderate, weak, none, insufficient data); ties: smaller regional p-value, then larger |standardized_change|, then variable id. A second ordering, by_magnitude, is exported next to it. The tier, p-value and effect_size of schema 1.1.0 are still exported.
methods.region_comparison: D(t) = A(t) - B(t), the difference of the two regions' deseasonalized fixed-mask monthly means on the months where both have a value; Sen's slope with 95% CI and Mann-Kendall (same autocorrelation handling as the regional trends) on D. 'trends differ' when p < alpha. P-values of the two regions are never compared, and overlapping confidence intervals are not used as a test. When the boxes overlap, the shared cells do not cancel in D: each mean is divided by its own total area weight (W_A, W_B), so a shared cell i enters D with weight w_i (1/W_A - 1/W_B), which is zero only when W_A = W_B.
methods.regional_mean: cos(latitude)-weighted mean over a fixed mask: the cells inside the box with data in at least 95% of the months, the same cells every month; a month is missing when more than 5% of the mask's area weight has no data
methods.rounding: every number rounded to 4 significant digits
methods.trend_estimator: Sen's slope, reported per decade in the variable's units

quality_gate.rule:
QUALITY GATE v1, unit = one (variable, region) pair, status = published | limited | held
G0 pipeline: a variable failing any step-1 check (source units, 297 consecutive months, NaN pattern,
   raw-vs-regridded, validate --source real) -> all its pairs held.
G1 data: fixed mask with 0 cells, or valid months < 95% of months -> held ("no data").
G2 reference trend check, fixed primary reference per variable (same cells, common months, anomalies,
   trendkit trend_report on each, D = product - reference via compare_pair, alpha 0.05;
   verdict = increasing / decreasing when p < 0.05, else no clear trend):
     verdicts differ and D significant        -> held     ("disagrees with <ref>")
     verdicts differ, D not significant       -> limited  ("verdict differs from <ref>, difference not significant")
     verdicts equal, D significant            -> limited  ("direction agrees with <ref>, size differs")
     verdicts equal, D not significant        -> published
   soil moisture (reference in other units, no D): verdicts differ -> held; equal -> limited.
   no reference cells in the region         -> limited  ("not checked against a reference")
G3 coverage of the check: reference cells cover < 50% of the product's cells in the region (area)
   -> at most limited ("checked on X% of the region").
G4 independence: reference not independent of the product -> at most limited (owner: on, 2026-11-15).
G5 t2m: nothing published without explicit owner approval (standing rule), whatever the gate says.
G6 region comparisons (compare/<variable>.json): a pair A-B gets the worse status of A and B.
Primary references: t2m GISTEMP v4 250 km land-only (independent, stations);
   precip GPCP v3.3 (related: IMERG Final is calibrated to GPCP); evap, runoff_surface, soil moisture
   MERRA-2 land M2TMNXLND EVLAND / RUNOFF / SFMC (other model and forcing; RUNOFF includes throughflow;
   SFMC is volumetric surface layer).
